person_made_it: David's own edition: his name, his colour, his half of the duel, his hello line, and the race laid out as a pit wall readout because he is the one who reads a room from the rail; the numbers are the real Friday qualifying and standings, spoiler-free.
emcee_who_is_speaking: The instruments speak: pole, leader, risk stacked as three panes before a single sentence, then Darby's briefing, then Gordon's challenge at the end.
what_time_of_day_is_this_room: Night shift at the pit wall: indigo ground, scan lines, translucent rotated panes in pink, teal and gold, the Greiman idiom of layered systems.
did_the_click_pay_me: Confirming as David plays his voice line and prints his cockpit assignment, the countdown reads as telemetry, picks lock on the phone, the two illustrations sit in bordered instrument frames, and the game link starts a race with sectors and deltas.
works_for_the_recipient: Google Fonts load Chakra Petch and Archivo with a system fallback stack, the page reads with scripts off as plain panes and a table, and every number is the same as the shared programme so the two never disagree.
taught_me_something: The readout format forced the five plays into five lines of data, and the fifth line is the new physics: active aero means no DRS train, which is the single thing that changes how this race will look.
told_me_the_truth: Verstappen's grid effect is marked unconfirmed, the strategy line stops where Formula 1's paywall stopped, and the sources sit behind a spoiler warning because live sites show the result now.
weakest: The rotated panes are a static gesture; a true Greiman layer would let David drag the panes and reorder his own readout, which is a next version.
